item.title: The Last Ship from the Falklands War Could Soon Be Scrapped
item.description: The RFA Argus, a British casualty receiving ship, is slated for retirement, then scrapping—but the Royal Navy has repeatedly dragged its heels on sending the ship to its grave. The post The Last Ship from the Falklands War Could Soon Be Scrapped appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Denmark Sold Its F-16s to Argentina Last Year. It Just Gave the Money to Ukraine.
item.description: The United States probably preferred the Danish sale to Argentina over a gift to Ukraine outright, as Buenos Aires is now tied to the US-made fighter jet. The post Denmark Sold Its F-16s to Argentina Last Year. It Just Gave the Money to Ukraine. appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Before It Gets Bigger, the US Navy Is Getting Smaller
item.description: This year, the US Navy has retired a handful of aging ships without immediate successors—shrinking its overall size, even amidst plans to expand it. The post Before It Gets Bigger, the US Navy Is Getting Smaller appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Who Will Succeed Ali Khamenei in Iran?
item.description: Ali Khamenei has dominated Iran’s clerical system for nearly four decades and sidelined all potential rivals—meaning there is no obvious choice for his successor. The post Who Will Succeed Ali Khamenei in Iran? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Why the US Keeps Misreading Iran’s Place on the Map
item.description: As long as Washington sees Iran at the edge of the Middle East rather than the center of “West Asia,” it will continue to fall prey to miscalculations. The post Why the US Keeps Misreading Iran’s Place on the Map appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Two Redlines for a Post-Islamic Republic Iran
item.description: With the death of Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the temptation is strong to redraw Iran’s borders or install a friendly despot. The US should resist it. The post Two Redlines for a Post-Islamic Republic Iran appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: What Exactly Is an “Integrated Air Defense System”?
item.description: IADS systems are the backbone of “anti-access/area denial” (A2/AD) networks, which all major world powers are pursuing in order to defend their airspaces. The post What Exactly Is an “Integrated Air Defense System”? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Is Indonesia the Next Rising Power in the Indo-Pacific?
item.description: Indonesia is seeking to modernize its military amid growing regional challenges—but is hamstrung by its paltry defense budget. The post Is Indonesia the Next Rising Power in the Indo-Pacific? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: Is Ireland Finally Investing in Its Own Defense?
item.description: Ireland is not a member of NATO, and invests only 0.2 percent of its GDP in defense—leading to widespread accusations of "free-riding" on European security guarantees. The post Is Ireland Finally Investing in Its Own Defense? appeared first on The National Interest.

item.title: How the US Can Sustain Deterrence After Khamenei
item.description: The end of the Islamic Republic is a tremendous opportunity for Iran and poses serious risks for regional stability. The United States should be prepared. The post How the US Can Sustain Deterrence After Khamenei appeared first on The National Interest.
